summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism, To Be a Christian, teaches that no one can save themselves, since sin has corrupted the conscience, confused the mind and captured the will; only God can save. God forgives sins and reconciles people to himself through his Son, given to the world as an undeserved gift of love, and there is salvation in no one else. The response is to repent and put faith in Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord: faith means believing the Gospel, entrusting oneself to him as Savior and obeying him as Lord. God grants reconciliation, forgiveness, union with Christ and adoption. The questions read do not speak of election or of whether believers can fall away.

points.question: Can people save themselves?
points.answer: No. Sin has corrupted the conscience, confused the mind and captured the will; only God can save.

points.question: How is a person saved?
points.answer: God forgives sins and reconciles people to himself through his Son, given as an undeserved gift of love. The response is to repent and put faith in Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord; faith means believing the Gospel, entrusting oneself to him as Savior and obeying him as Lord.
